spans.s: (I)--a son of आन्ध्र Ha1leya, and father of पुरीषभीरु. भा.
--slapping of arms in defiance by कृष्ण on seeing the असुर अरिष्ट as a bull. Vi. V. १४. 8.
--one of the ten daughters of रौद्राश्व. वा. ९९. १२६.
(I)--span, employed in describing measurement in iconography; nine तालस् generally for deities, दानवस् and kinnaras; measurement made usually by the middle finger. Br.
(II) (च्)--kingdom watered by the R. चक्ष. Br. II. १८. ४६.
(III)--a hell into which falls one, who murders a क्षत्रिय or वैश्य or Brahmana, or one who defiles a precep- tor's bed. Br.

--an underworld, being the residence of Asura Maya who won the grace of शिव and moved about without fear of the सुदर्शन;
1: भा.

. २६; V. २४. 7 and २८.
residence of प्रह्लाद.
2: Br. II. २०. १२-14, २५-31.

. १६; वा. ६८. १६.
station- ed at the northern gate of the शून्यक city with ten अक्षौ- हिणिस्.
2: Br. IV. २२. २५.
(II)--the palm tree as the banner of Bala- deva. Vi.
--the Asura who was stationed at the western gate of the शून्यक city with ten अक्षौहिणि soldiers. Br. IV. २२. २४. [page२-023+ ३३]

(I)--the son of Jayadhvaja and father of one hundred sons (तालजन्घस्--वीतिहोत्र being the elder). The तालजन्घ line came to an end by Aurva's power.
1: भा. IX. २३. २८; M. ४३. ४७; वा. ८८. १२२; ९४. ५०.
Afraid of परशुराम he escaped to the Himalayas and returned after peace was restored. Led an expedition to अयोध्या whose king Phalgutantra fled with his wife and child;
2: Br. III. ६९. ५१; ४७. ६७, ७८.
defeated बाहु, but was defeated by his own son,

--a class of क्षत्रियस् defeated by Sagara;
1: भा.

; २३. २८.
the collective name of the १०० sons of तालजन्घ and a Haihaya clan; of them five गणस् could be distinguished; वीतिहोत्र, Bhoja, Avantya, तुण्डिकेर and तालजन्घ.
2: Br. III. ४८. २३-5; ६३. १२० and १३४; ६९. ५१-3; M. ४३. ४८; वा. ९४. ५१-2.
--the Asura stationed at the eastern gate of the शून्यक city with ten अक्षौहिणि soldiers. Br. IV. २२. २२.
--the Asura stationed at the southern gate of the शून्यक city with ten अक्षौहिणि soldiers. Br. IV. २२. २३.
--a grove of palms near ब्रिन्दावन where lived the demon Dhenuka who was killed by राम and कृष्ण. Vi.
